description: Blocks an EnterWorktree(path=...) call that targets a worktree a DIFFERENT agent created. CC names a dispatched subagent's isolated worktree `.claude/worktrees/agent-<agent_id>`; this hook extracts `<id>` from `args.path` and compares it against the CALLING agent's own top-level `agent_id` (T2-trustworthy, forged args.agent_id dropped) — a mismatch, or the orchestrator (no agent_id) targeting any agent-<id> worktree, is BLOCKED. EnterWorktree's own validation only confirms the path is a real worktree of the repo (git worktree list), never that the caller owns it, and reaching into a foreign one has repeatedly reported SUCCESS then permanently bricked the calling agent's Bash tool for the rest of its session with no recovery path (not even ExitWorktree) -- at least 4 confirmed occurrences, HYP-1384's retrospective. Creating a brand-new worktree (the `name` argument, no `path`) is untouched -- always the caller's own. A path that does not match the agent-<id> convention at all is allowed (fail-open on an unfamiliar naming scheme rather than guessing). Deny-by-default: no self-service bypass; a would-be BLOCK consults RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_ENTERWORKTREE_FOREIGN_GUARD with a written justification, which asks Telegram via trusted tg-ctl and allows ONLY on an approval tap (a blank/bare 1 denies). timeout_ms 960000 covers tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus margin so a hung ask can't race the dispatcher's timeout kill into a silent on_error=open ALLOW; a CC settings entry launching cc_hook_bridge must set timeout >960s. on_error=open. Registration note: firing requires a rig-cli `EnterWorktree` PreToolUse matcher (see lib/cc_hook_bridge/README.md's Extensibility section) -- the point mapping alone is inert until that matcher ships / rig apply runs.
